findings.summary: AxiosError.from copies only message, code and name instead of all own properties, so errno, syscall, address, port, response and the original stack are lost.
from(null) or from(undefined) now throws a TypeError because error.message is read without a guard; the old code fell back to 'Error'.
cause and isAxiosError are now enumerable own properties, so they show up in Object.keys, spreads, Object.assign, toFlatObject and deep-equality checks.
status is assigned response.status directly and can now be undefined instead of null, which breaks status === null checks.
__CANCEL__ moved from the prototype to an enumerable own instance property and is no longer on CanceledError.prototype.
The new tests only check isNativeError and the static error codes. They don't cover from() with extra properties, a null error, or a response with no status.
